# Open the model you validated in Basic {.center}

::: {.notes}
Voce docente (IT): apertura. L'arco RIAPRE il modello validato in Basic — non si
ricostruisce nulla. Quattro tappe: interpretare (VIMP/SHAP) → deep learning (torch/
luz/brulee) → `ellmer` come ETL tipizzato → capstone `targets`. torch è pre-riscaldato
nello step 00 (`torch_tensor(1)`), così il primo tensore non paga l'init. Numeri
reali da ricordare: l'RF di Basic sta a CV AUC-ROC ~0.79; VIMP mette in cima
ejection_fraction / serum_creatinine. NON vendere l'MLP come vincitore della foresta.
:::

The model you built in Basic is not the end — it is the **subject**. We **open** the
random forest you built and validated in Basic, then push past it.

- **Interpret it** — permutation VIMP and agnostic SHAP, anchored on a logistic regression.
- **Go deep** — a live `brulee` MLP (`torch` / `luz` / `brulee`), then CNN/RNN/fused nets written (not trained).
- **Reach an LLM** — `ellmer` as a typed, reproducible LLM-as-ETL.
- **Seal it** — a `targets` pipeline that re-derives the explanation, all-skip on re-run.

Everything live-coded; nothing pre-baked is shown as live (one labeled exception).

# Step 00 · Recap & setup {#sec-00-recap .center}

<!-- Step 00 (demo, 12 min): reload Basic's finalized workflow; predict 1 row; pre-warm torch. -->

**Objective.** Reopen the validated model — without retraining.

- Reload Basic's finalized random forest: `extract_workflow(readRDS("final_fit.rds"))`.
- `predict()` on **one** patient row — a probability, not yet an explanation.
- **Pre-warm torch** so the first tensor later does not pay the init cost.

::: {.notes}
Voce docente (IT): demo (~12 min). Si RICARICA, non si riaddestra. Live-check al
min 10: reload + `predict` su 1 riga + `torch_tensor(1)` SENZA download (torch caldo).
GREEN/RED. Su questa macchina di build `cuda_is_available()` è FALSE; in aula, sulla
NVIDIA, è TRUE. Il punto: una probabilità non è una spiegazione → apre lo step 01.
:::

# Step 01 · Interpretability {#sec-01-interpret .center}

<!-- Step 01 (hands-on, 48 min): permutation VIMP (logistic+RF); agnostic SHAP (anchor + 1 RF row); logistic as sanity. -->

**Objectives.** Open the black box with two model-agnostic tools.

- **Permutation VIMP** (`{vip}`): shuffle a predictor $\to$ how far AUC-ROC drops = how much
  the model **relies** on it. Reliance, **not** causation.
- **Agnostic SHAP** via **`kernelshap` + `shapviz`**: attribute one prediction across features.
- The **same explainer line** runs on logistic $\to$ RF $\to$ MLP — only the model object changes.

::: {.notes}
Voce docente (IT): hands-on (~48 min), zona di rischio per profondità. Min-24 (MCQ):
VIMP = reliance, NON causazione / coefficiente con segno / p-value. Numero reale di
build: la VIMP a permutazione mette in cima ejection_fraction e serum_creatinine (con
age) — i predittori clinicamente sensati, con effetti soglia/non-monotoni. Sono le
feature che la foresta ha imparato a USARE, non un'affermazione causale né di direzione.
:::

## The logistic anchor — SHAP must recover what we already know {.smaller}

Before pointing SHAP at the opaque forest, we **anchor** it on a logistic regression —
a model we *can* read off its coefficients.

- Run SHAP on the **linear anchor** with `permshap()` (near-**exact** Shapley values).
- The SHAP attributions must **echo the fitted coefficients** — same leading features,
  consistent signs. If they did not, we would not trust SHAP on the forest.
- Build reality: **ejection_fraction**, **age**, **serum_creatinine** lead *both* the
  waterfall and the largest-magnitude coefficients.

Then the agnosticism payoff: the **same** call points at the random forest (no coefficients
at all) — `kernelshap()` for the forest, `permshap()` reserved for the linear anchor.

::: {.notes}
Voce docente (IT): predict-output al min-38 — che forma ha lo SHAP rispetto ai
coefficienti logistici? Perché rassicura PRIMA di puntare l'RF: l'agnostico deve
*recuperare* il noto. permshap() = esatto sul lineare (il sanity-check più pulito);
kernelshap() = ibrido sull'RF (11 feature, scelta pratica). "Your turn" min-66: la
stessa riga del blocco 01 puntata sull'RF — cambia solo l'oggetto-modello.
:::

## SHAP knobs — variance vs. cost {.smaller}

<!-- PARAMS_I node — replaces the old "nsim" framing; we use kernelshap now. -->

Three knobs govern an agnostic SHAP run. None of them is a quality dial.

| knob | what it is | the tradeoff |
|---|---|---|
| **background** (`bg_X`) | reference rows SHAP integrates over | larger $\to$ lower-variance attributions, **higher cost**; tiny $\to$ cheap but noisier |
| **which rows** (`X`) | the patients you explain | a waterfall explains **one** row; pick the case(s) you actually care about |
| **exact vs. sampling** | how Shapley values are computed | `permshap()` **exact** for small $p$ / the linear anchor; `kernelshap()` hybrid/sampling as $p$ (the number of features) grows |

- Smaller background is **not** "more accurate" — it is **cheaper and noisier**.
- With 11 features the exact enumeration gets expensive $\to$ the forest uses the hybrid `kernelshap()`.

::: {.notes}
Voce docente (IT): min-46 (MCQ). Sostituisce il vecchio framing "nsim" — ora si usa
kernelshap (override 2026-05-31, §11). Lezione invariata: varianza-vs-costo. Distrattori
adattati: "meno background = più accurato" (NO, più rumoroso), "background conta solo per
alberi" (NO, è agnostico), "X = numero di feature" (NO, sono le righe da spiegare).
permshap esatto sull'ancora lineare, kernelshap ibrido come p cresce.
:::

# Step 02 · Deep learning {#sec-02-deep-learning .center}

<!-- Step 02 (hands-on + demo, 67 min): MLP knobs -> train MLP live + SHAP callback -> write CNN/RNN/fused (shape-check) -> GPU-vs-CPU -> option B. -->

**Objectives.** Train one net honestly; write the rest.

- **Knobs first**, then train a small `brulee` **MLP live** (≤30 epochs, seconds).
- Explain it with the **same agnostic SHAP line** — only the model object changed.
- Write **CNN / RNN / fused** `nn_module`s — validated by a `forward()` **shape-check** (`[5, 2]`), **not trained**.
- **GPU-vs-CPU** on the heavy workload; the **one** labeled option-B loss curve.

::: {.notes}
Voce docente (IT): hands-on + demo (~67 min), l'hotspot (9 chunk). Le slide-parametro
PRECEDONO il train. L'MLP è addestrato DAVVERO dal vivo: il suo `roc_auc` è single-split,
NON confrontabile con la CV ~0.79 della foresta (apples-to-oranges — non dire che la rete
batte la foresta). CNN/RNN/fused = SCRITTE non addestrate, validate solo dallo shape-check
`[5,2]`. SHAP riusato al min-66 = riuso intenzionale, non nuovo carico.
:::

## MLP knobs — and the overfit cure {.smaller}

<!-- PARAMS_DL node. The param slide precedes the train. -->

A small `brulee` MLP has four primary knobs (plus two minor). With generous defaults a small
net **overfits** this 299-patient cohort — and the cure is always the same.

| knob | what it controls | bias / variance |
|---|---|---|
| `epochs` | how long it trains | too many $\to$ fits noise (**overfit**) |
| `learn_rate` | step size of each update | too high $\to$ diverges; too low $\to$ underfits in budget |
| `hidden_units` | capacity (width) | more $\to$ lower bias, **higher variance** |
| `penalty` | weight decay (regularization) | $\uparrow$ penalty $\to$ more bias, **less variance** |

- Minor knobs: `batch` (gradient noise) and `activation` (nonlinearity) — **not** regularizers.
- **Overfit cure:** turn `penalty` **up** and `hidden_units` **down** (or cut `epochs`).

::: {.notes}
Voce docente (IT): min-60 (MCQ). MLP overfit → quale knob? ✓ penalty↑ / hidden↓.
Distrattori: "più epoche" (peggiora), "learning-rate↑" (diverge), "cambia activation
come regolarizzatore" (NO, l'activation non regolarizza). Fallo dal vivo cambiando UN
solo numero. La slide-parametro viene PRIMA del train (knob pre-caricati).
:::

## CNN / RNN / fused — written, not trained {.smaller}

<!-- NNMOD/CNN/RNN/FUSED nodes — Parsons reorder, min-80. -->

Three richer `nn_module`s, **written not trained** — validated only by a `forward()` shape-check.

| net | the knobs | shape role |
|---|---|---|
| **1D-CNN** | `kernel` / `stride` / `channels` | slides a filter over a signal |
| **RNN** | `hidden` / `sequence` / LSTM-GRU | reads a vitals sequence over time |
| **fused** | 3 branches $\to$ `torch_cat(dim = 2)` $\to$ head | branch widths must **sum** to the head input |

- The fused net runs all three branches and concatenates them along `dim = 2` into a two-logit head.
- A correct **`[5, 2]`** out (five patients, two logits) proves the wiring — it claims **nothing** about accuracy.

::: {.notes}
Voce docente (IT): min-80 (Parsons). Riordina il `forward()` della rete fusa: 3 rami →
`torch_cat(list(t, c, r), dim = 2)` → head. Vincolo fisso: prima calcoli i rami, POI
concat-e-head; la larghezza d'ingresso della head = somma delle larghezze dei 3 rami.
Lo split scrivi-non-addestra collassa CNN+RNN+fused in UN solo schema ("modulo cablato
dal forward") → da 9 a ~5 chunk effettivi. Nessun training: solo `[5,2]`.
:::

## The honesty rule — one labeled exception {.smaller}

<!-- HONESTY node, min-92. -->

Everything on screen is either **live** or **declared write-only**. The doctrine is explicit.

- The MLP above is **trained live**; its `roc_auc` is a genuine held-out number.
- The CNN/RNN/fused nets are **shape-checked write-only** — never presented as trained.
- The GPU demo's killed CPU epoch **was live** — a real interrupted epoch, not a simulation.

::: {.fragment .callout-warning appearance="simple"}
**The one labeled exception.** The fused-net **loss curve** is pre-computed — *"I trained
this earlier on GPU."* It is labeled in the plot title and is the **only** pre-baked result.
:::

::: {.fragment .callout-note appearance="simple"}
**`targets` is not an exception.** A cached target re-shown as *"skip"* is **reproducibility**
(re-derivable, hash-checked: same input $\Rightarrow$ same output), not fakery — conceptually
the opposite of a pre-baked number shown as live.
:::

::: {.notes}
Voce docente (IT): min-92 (MCQ). ✓ unica eccezione ETICHETTATA = la loss-curve opzione B;
la CPU killata ERA live. Distrattori: "nessuna cache mai" (NO), "tutto DL pre-trainabile
senza label" (NO), "identico al cache di targets" (NO — la riproducibilità hash-checked è
un'altra cosa). Distinzione chiave da far atterrare prima del capstone.
:::

## GPU payoff — where the accelerator actually pays {.smaller}

The accelerator is **not** a magic speed button. Match it to the workload.

- The tiny tabular **MLP does not need a GPU** — it trains in seconds on a CPU (overhead would lose).
- The payoff is on the **CNN / fused** workload, where the per-epoch cost actually bites.
- The live classroom move: **start on CPU $\to$ watch one epoch crawl $\to$ kill it $\to$ rerun on GPU.**
- Authored **write-only** (`#| eval: false`): it runs on the classroom NVIDIA/CUDA machine,
  where `cuda_is_available()` is `TRUE` — not on this CPU build box (`FALSE`).

::: {.notes}
Voce docente (IT): non vendere la GPU sul giocattolo (MLP minuscolo), vendila sul carico
vero (CNN/fuso). L'epoca CPU "uccisa" è un'epoca reale interrotta, non simulata: parte sul
serio, arranca, la fermi → rerun con `cpu = FALSE`, stesso codice, cambia solo
l'acceleratore. Su questa macchina di build gira solo in lettura (eval false).
:::

# Step 03 · LLM as typed ETL {#sec-03-ellmer .center}

<!-- Step 03 (hands-on, 36 min): type_object schema; ONE live extraction; batch map written-not-run; temperature 0. -->

**Objectives.** Turn an LLM into a reproducible ETL, not a chat.

- A **typed schema** (`type_object()`) is the **contract**: declare fields + R types $\to$
  every note comes back as the same validated record.
- **One** live structured extraction (first note); the batch `purrr::map` is **written, not run**.
- `temperature = 0` = **deterministic** ETL (same input $\to$ same record).

::: {.notes}
Voce docente (IT): hands-on (~36 min). L'LLM NON è una chat: è un ETL tipizzato e
riproducibile. Min-112 (predict-output): struttura del record `type_object()` — 4 campi
(age integer, ejection_fraction number, on_betablocker boolean, primary_dx enum a 4 valori)
+ cosa fa l'enum se il campo manca (vincola a lista chiusa; opzionali → NA, record resta
valido). Modello reale: gpt-5.4-nano. Una sola estrazione live, il batch map è write-only.
:::

## The schema is the contract {.smaller}

A chat returns prose you must re-parse; an **ETL returns a record**. The schema is the difference.

- `type_object()` declares each field + its R type — e.g. `age = type_integer("patient age in years")`.
- An **enum** (`type_enum`) is a guard rail: `primary_dx` can only be one of a closed list, never `"probably cardiomyopathy"`.
- Optional fields (EF not stated, beta-blocker not mentioned) come back as **`NA`** — the record stays valid.
- The batch is **written, not run**: `map()` iterates note-by-note into a tidy tibble; `temperature = 0` keeps it deterministic.

::: {.fragment .callout-note appearance="simple"}
**Honesty (carried forward).** With no API key, we show a **labeled cached** result from an
earlier live run — never a faked record. The key lives only in a gitignored `.Renviron`.
:::

::: {.notes}
Voce docente (IT): min-124 (MCQ). temperature bassa + `map`: ✓ determinismo (ETL) +
iterazione elemento-per-elemento. Distrattori: "temp = qualità" (NO), "temp alta + map su
GPU" (NO), "temp irrilevante per extraction" (NO). La cache etichettata è la stessa
dottrina dell'opzione-B: un vero record salvato prima, mostrato con etichetta, mai finto.
:::

# Step 04 · Reproducibility capstone {#sec-04-targets .center}

<!-- Step 04 (demo, 20 min): read the targets DAG (tar_visnetwork); first build runs; re-run all-skip. -->

**Objectives.** Make the whole story reproducible by construction.

- Read the `targets` **DAG** (`tar_visnetwork()`): `cohort_file` $\to$ `cohort`, `model_file` $\to$ `model`,
  and `model + cohort` $\to$ `explanation`.
- The `explanation` target is the **bridge**: it reloads the Basic RF and re-derives its VIMP.
- A **second** `tar_make()` is **all-skip** — input hashes unchanged ⇒ reproducibility, not fakery.

::: {.notes}
Voce docente (IT): capstone (~20 min, demo). Min-138 (predict-output): predire che il 2°
`tar_make()` riporti "skip" ovunque + ragione (hash degli input invariati). PROVA col
valore di ritorno, non col messaggio: `tar_outdated()` == character(0) e `tar_progress()`
= tutti "skipped" (5 target). Il bridge `explanation` ricalcola DAVVERO la VIMP della RF
ricaricata → stesso ordine: ejection_fraction / serum_creatinine / age. Stretch Davide:
il device GPU è un input CIECO se non è un target (targets non lo hash-a).
:::

## You can hand this pipeline to a peer {.center}

The capstone payoff: this **reproducible explain $\to$ deep $\to$ LLM** pipeline is sealed.

- A peer can clone the folder, run `tar_make()`, and re-derive the **same** explanation of
  the Basic model — deterministically, hash-checked.
- Basic **promised** that Advanced would reload its validated model. **We delivered:** day one
  reopened that exact `final_fit`, and we never retrained it.

The loop is closed — from a validated model to a reproducible pipeline a colleague can re-run.

::: {.notes}
Voce docente (IT): chiusura. Chiude il loop Basic↔Advanced: Basic prometteva che Advanced
RICARICA il modello (pre-hook), e l'abbiamo mantenuto — step 00 ha riaperto `final_fit`
senza retrain. Il payoff finale è la consegnabilità: la pipeline spiegata-deep-LLM è
riproducibile da un terzo via `targets`. Niente riferimenti temporali, niente nomi oltre
Corrado Lanera (UBEP).
:::

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}

**Interpretability & deep learning (free, online)**

- **Molnar.** *Interpretable Machine Learning* — `christophm.github.io/interpretable-ml-book`. SHAP and permutation importance — the foundations of step 01.
- **`torch` for R** · **`luz`** · **`brulee`** — `torch.mlverse.org`. The deep-learning stack we used live.
- **Chollet & Allaire.** *Deep Learning with R* (2e) — for the curious, beyond `brulee`.

:::
::: {.column width="50%"}

**LLMs & reproducible pipelines**

- **`ellmer`** — `ellmer.tidyverse.org`. Typed, structured LLM calls (our LLM-as-ETL).
- **Landau.** *The `targets` R package user manual* — `books.ropensci.org/targets`. The capstone pipeline.
- **`kernelshap` + `shapviz`** (M. Mayer) — the agnostic SHAP tooling of step 01.
- **Kuhn & Silge.** *Tidy Modeling with R* — `tmwr.org` (shared with Basic).

:::
